text:
### Observed differences

- The dominant difference is a near-complete reversal of execution order between two neighbouring groups of activities. In the earlier window, a case ran A40, then one of the alternatives A19, A21 or A24 (each in about 30–36 of 100 cases), then A25 and A29, then the trio A20, A22, A23 — present in every case, in varying internal order — and finally A30: A40 led to A21 at the very next event in about 94 in 100 of the pair's appearances, A19/A21/A24 each led to A25 in about 93–97 in 100 of their outgoing transitions, A29 led to A20/A22/A23 in roughly equal thirds, and each trio member led on to A30 in about 29–37 in 100. In the later window this is inverted: A40 leads into the trio (A40 followed by A22 within one to three events in about 200 of 200 cases, versus about 1 of 200 before), the trio continues to A25 (about 28–37 in 100 of each member's outgoing transitions, where previously a similar share went to A30), A29 leads to one of A24, A19, A21 (about 38, 32 and 28 in 100), and that alternative then leads to A30 (about 92–97 in 100, typically at the next event). [DIR013, LAG027, LAG019, DIR006, DIR008, DIR011, DIR012, DIR007, DIR009, DIR010, LAG028, LAG018, LAG020, LAG025]

- The pair-wise order relations flip almost completely rather than partially: A25 preceded A20, A22 and A23 in about 97–99 of 100 co-occurrences before and followed them in about 97–99 of 100 after; the same near-complete reversal holds between A29 and the trio, between A19 and the trio and A25/A29, and between A21 or A24 and the trio and A25/A29 (for example, A24 ran before A20 in about 36 of 100 before, and A20 ran before A24 in about 39 of 100 after). [REL023, REL024, REL031, REL016, REL021, REL022, REL035]

- Distances and positions shift accordingly. A40 to A25 widened from typically two events apart (about 91 in 100) to four (about 78 in 100), while A29 to A30 narrowed from four (about 94 in 100) to two (about 94 in 100); A22 or A23 followed by A30 within five events fell from about 200 to 1 of 200 cases, while A22 or A23 followed by A25 rose from about 1 to 200. Mean event position (as a fraction of the trace) moved from about 0.64 to about 0.38 for A20, A22 and A23, and from about 0.37 to about 0.67 for A19, A21 and A24, while A25 and A29 shifted only slightly later (about 0.39 to 0.45, and 0.58 to 0.64). [LAG029, LAG026, LAG022, LAG024, LAG021, LAG023, POS003, POS005, POS006, POS002, POS004, POS007, POS008, POS009]

- Separately, A08 became much rarer: it appeared in about 64 of 100 traces before and about 29 of 100 after. Before, it typically sat between A15 and A16 (about 39 of A15's outgoing transitions in 100 went to A08 and about 61 to A16; A08 led to A16 in about 93 of 100, usually immediately). After, A15 continues directly to A16 in about 88 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 7 to A08), and A08's own continuations are spread thinly over many activities (largest single share about 31 in 100, to A16). [POS001, REL002, DIR005, DIR002, LAG001, LAG009]

- Smaller differences: the continuations at A14, A43 and A45 became slightly less deterministic (A14 to A15 about 98 to 80 in 100 of outgoing transitions, A43 to A44 about 96 to 85, A45 to A46 about 97 to 83, with the immediate one-step gap falling from about 98 to 84 in 100), and the flagged profiles of the rare activities A04 and A10 rest on only about 13–44 and 16–40 traces. [DIR004, DIR014, DIR015, LAG030, DIR001, DIR003]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two adjacent segments of the process exchanged their order. In the earlier window the choice step — one of A19, A21 or A24 — ran between A40 and A25, and the three-activity passage A20/A22/A23 ran between A29 and A30; in the later window A20, A22 and A23 run between A40 and A25, and the choice among A19/A21/A24 runs between A29 and A30, with the A25/A29 passage keeping its place in the middle. Participation is essentially unchanged — the trio, A25 and A29 still occur in every trace, and each alternative still occurs in about three of ten traces — which fits a reordering rather than activities being added, removed or made optional. [REL023, REL024, DIR012, DIR013, POS003, POS008, POS002, POS004, POS007]

The change is shown directly and consistently: roughly thirty activity pairs invert their dominant order almost completely (for example, A25 before A20 in about 98 of 100 before, A20 before A25 in about 97 of 100 after), and these reversals are facets of one underlying exchange rather than independent shifts; the successor profiles rewire in the predicted direction at A19/A21/A24 (from A25 to A30), at A20/A22/A23 (from A30 to A25), at A29 and at A40; and event distances move exactly as the exchange predicts (A40 to A25 two then four events apart; A29 to A30 four then two). With 90 flagged items against roughly 0.84 expected if nothing had changed, sampling variation cannot account for the pattern as a whole. [REL016, REL021, REL023, REL035, DIR006, DIR011, DIR007, DIR010, DIR012, DIR013, LAG029, LAG026]

A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a gradual transition: the windows are aggregates, so an exchange phased in across the boundary looks identical to a single switchover. Positions and gaps are event positions rather than clock times, so the evidence constrains sequence only, and the mixed internal order of A20/A22/A23 — each can follow the others in both windows — cannot be characterised further. [DIR007, DIR009, DIR010, POS003]

Other differences: the A08 detour between A15 and A16 is now usually skipped — A08 appears in about 29 of 100 traces (about 64 before), A15 continues straight to A16 in about 88 of 100 of its outgoing transitions (about 61 before), and A08's remaining continuations are spread over many activities (largest share about 31 in 100 to A16, versus about 93 before). Minor: continuations at A14, A43 and A45 became slightly less deterministic. [POS001, DIR005, DIR002, LAG001, DIR004, DIR014, DIR015]
